mainTopic: Why the comb משנה is not followed, and the rules of the three-month wait before betrothal and marriage
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about whether the הלכה always follows a סתם משנה, a ruling in the משנה stated with no name attached. A challenge is raised from an unnamed משנה in כלים about broken combs, which we do not follow. The answer is that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש called it 'not a משנה'. The גמרא tries two contradictions inside that משנה to explain why, and both are answered. The real reason turns out to be that careful teachers end it with 'This is רבי שמעון', so it is one Sage's view. Then the גמרא turns to the three-month wait before a woman may remarry. It rules that betrothal is allowed during those months, discusses whether day 90 is enough, and gives the final rule: neither the first day nor the betrothal day counts. Finally, a קל וחומר from the mourning before תשעה באב leads the גמרא to change רבי יוסי's wording. A widow may not marry during her three months, but she may get betrothed.

steps.title: The ברייתא's unnamed ruling really comes from רבי's משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on a proof from an unnamed ruling in a ברייתא. רבי חייא got that ruling from רבי's משנה, so it carries no extra weight of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רבי had not taught it in the משנה, where would רבי חייא have gotten it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is rejecting a proof that relied on a ruling stated without a name in a ברייתא. It argues that this ruling is just taken from רבי's משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא was רבי's student and organized the ברייתות based on his teacher's material. So if רבי חייא writes a ruling with no name attached, that only shows which opinion from the משנה he chose to follow. It does not prove the ruling is the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: where would he get it from?

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a question in form, but it is not really asking anything. It is a rhetorical argument meaning: obviously רבי חייא got it from רבי.

phrases.english: And if רבי did not teach it,
from where would רבי חייא know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי רַבִּי לֹא שְׁנָאָהּ, רַבִּי חִיָּיא מִנַּיִן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this piece by weakening a proof taken from an unnamed ruling in a ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating the ברייתא's unnamed ruling as an independent sign of the accepted הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's ruling is drawn from רבי's משנה, so it only shows that רבי חייא sided with that opinion.

steps.title: Quoting an unnamed משנה about broken combs
steps.stepSummary: The questioner quotes a long unnamed משנה from מסכת כלים about combs for flax and wool that lost their teeth. This sets up his challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But we learned in a משנה: A comb for flax that lost its teeth, and two teeth are left, can become טמא. If one is left, it stays טהור. And each tooth taken out on its own can become טמא. A comb for wool that lost every other tooth stays טהור. If three teeth are left in one place, it can become טמא. If one of those three is the outer edge, it stays טהור. If two teeth were taken out and made into tweezers, they can become טמא. If one tooth was taken out and fixed up for a lamp or for stretching, it can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner quotes a full משנה with no name attached. He is setting up his next move: he is about to show that we do not rule like this unnamed משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The underlying rule is that an item can only become טמא if it still counts as a usable כלי. A comb with enough teeth left still works, so it can become טמא. A single loose tooth that can still serve some purpose also counts as a כלי. The details matter less here than the fact that this whole משנה is stated with no name, so it is a סתם משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: but we learned in a משנה (opens a challenge)
can become ritually impure / stays ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the comb details. The גמרא is not studying combs here. It quotes this משנה only because it is a סתם משנה that we do not follow.

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: This is רבי נחום challenging רבי חייא, quoting the משנה in כלים 13:8.

phrases.english: A comb for flax whose teeth were removed,
and two remained in it — they can become impure,
and if one remained — it is pure.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ אַחַת אַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן — טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.english: And all of them that were removed one by one, on their own — can become impure.
phrases.notes: This is about the loose teeth themselves, after they were pulled out of the comb.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל צֶמֶר שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ שִׁינָּיו אַחַת מִבֵּינְתַיִם — טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: One for wool whose teeth were removed, every other one — it is pure.

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: If three remained in it in one place — it can become impure.
If the outer one was one of them — it is pure.
phrases.notes: The outer one is the edge piece of the comb's frame, so only two real teeth are left.

phrases.english: If two were removed and he made them into tweezers — they can become impure.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת וְהִתְקִינָהּ לְנֵר אוֹ לְמִיתּוּחַ — טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: If one, and he fixed it up for a lamp or for stretching — it can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the general rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the הלכה always follows a סתם משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup: it brings a clear example of a סתם משנה. The next step will show that we do not rule like it.

steps.title: But we do not rule like that משנה
steps.stepSummary: The punchline of the challenge: we hold that the הלכה does not follow this unnamed משנה, so the rule of סתם משנה seems broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that the הלכה is not like that משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the questioner delivers his challenge. Here is a סתם משנה that we do not follow, so how can we say the הלכה always follows a סתם משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step only quoted the source. This step adds the key fact: this unnamed משנה is not the accepted הלכה. If even one סתם משנה is not followed, the rule does not seem to be absolute.

keyTerms.meaning: and we have an accepted rule that

phrases.english: And we hold
that the הלכה is not like that משנה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַיְימָא לַן דְּאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּאוֹתָהּ מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that the משנה quote in step 2 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סתם משנה exists (the comb משנה) that we do not follow, so the rule cannot be absolute.

steps.title: That משנה is an exception: 'this is not a משנה'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the rule holds everywhere except this משנה, because רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both said it is not an authoritative משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave that one aside, because רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both said: This is not a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer defends the rule of סתם משנה. The comb משנה is a special case that two great אמוראים already set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not broken. This one משנה was declared 'not a משנה' by רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, so it never had the normal weight of a סתם משנה. Every other סתם משנה still sets the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: except for it, leave it aside
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה stands. The comb משנה in כלים is a known exception, because רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said 'זו אינה משנה'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'זו אינה משנה' does not mean the words are missing from the משנה. They are there. It means this משנה is not treated as an authority for deciding הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an exception can be explained without throwing away the general rule of סתם משנה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Except for that one,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: for רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say:
This is not a משנה.
phrases.notes: He means it is not a reliable משנה to rule from, even though it appears in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 2–3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenge to one exceptional source while keeping the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the comb משנה, it seemed that the rule of סתם משנה is not reliable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. The comb משנה is excluded because רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said 'זו אינה משנה'.

steps.title: Why is this משנה not authoritative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said the comb משנה is not authoritative.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this משנה is not considered authoritative. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 told us that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rejected this משנה, but not why. A סתם משנה normally sets the הלכה, so the גמרא wants to know what is wrong with this one.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said this משנה is not an authoritative one (step 4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the answer given in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rejected the comb משנה as authoritative.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה contradicts the last part
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, quoting רב אידי בריה דרב איקא, says the משנה contradicts itself. One part suggests two remaining teeth are enough to make the comb טמא. Another part says three are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אידי the son of רב איקא: because the first part contradicts the last part. The משנה teaches that a wool comb that lost every other tooth is טהור. That implies that if two teeth were left together in one place, it is טמא. But then it teaches that if three were left, it is טמא. Three, yes; two, no!
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא explains that the משנה is rejected because it seems to contradict itself about how many teeth must be left for the comb to stay a utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part implies that two teeth left side by side keep the comb a utensil, so it can become טמא. The later part says three teeth are needed, which implies two are not enough. A משנה that seems to say both things cannot be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part contradicts the last part
Ritually pure / able to become (or is) ritually impure
From in between, so every other one

steps.confusionAlert: A broken comb that is 'טהור' here does not mean it was purified. It means it is no longer a utensil, so it cannot pick up טומאה at all.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoach said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Idi son of Rav Ika:
Because the first clause contradicts the last clause.
For it teaches: a wool comb
whose teeth were removed, every other one, is pure.

phrases.aramaic: הָא נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בּוֹ שְׁתַּיִם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: This implies: if two remained in it in one place, it is impure,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: and then it teaches: if three remained in it, it is impure.
Three, yes; two, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by pointing to an internal contradiction in the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is rejected because its first and last clauses seem to contradict each other about whether two teeth are enough.

steps.title: Maybe inner teeth and outer teeth are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the contradiction: two teeth may be enough when they are inner teeth, while three are needed when they are outer teeth at the edge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what is the difficulty? Perhaps this ruling is about the inner teeth, and that ruling is about the outer teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claimed contradiction by saying the two clauses may be talking about different teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two inner teeth in the middle of the comb can still be used, so the comb stays a utensil. Outer teeth sit next to the frame and are harder to use, so there three are needed. If the clauses are about different cases, there is no contradiction, and this reason for rejecting the משנה falls away.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps this one is about the inner ones,
phrases.notes: The inner teeth in the middle of the comb, away from the frame.

phrases.english: and that one is about the outer ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the contradiction offered in step 6 by placing the two clauses in different cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the specific contradiction about two versus three teeth; the claim that the משנה is not authoritative still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction assumes both clauses are about the same teeth, but they may be about inner and outer teeth.

steps.title: A second contradiction: does a removed tooth need preparing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different contradiction. One clause says single teeth that were removed are טמא even without being prepared. The last clause implies a tooth is טמא only if it was prepared for a lamp or for stretching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the contradiction is from here. It teaches: all of them that were removed one by one on their own are טמא, even though he did not prepare them. Now say the last clause: one tooth that he prepared for a lamp or for stretching is טמא. If he prepared it, yes; if he did not prepare it, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the first contradiction and offers a new one from a different part of the same משנה, to explain why it is not authoritative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause implies that a single tooth counts as a utensil by itself, without any extra work. The last clause implies it counts as a utensil only once it was prepared for a use. That looks like a real contradiction inside the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (bringing a better source)
He prepared it (fixed it for use)

phrases.english: Rather, from here, for it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ אַחַת אַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן — טְמֵאוֹת,
phrases.english: And all of them that were removed one by one on their own are impure,
phrases.notes: He means the single teeth pulled out of the comb.

phrases.english: and that is even though he did not prepare it.
Say the last clause:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת וְהִתְקִינָהּ לְנֵר אוֹ לְמִיתּוּחַ — טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: One tooth that he prepared for a lamp or for stretching is impure.
If he prepared it, yes; if he did not prepare it, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 knocked down the first contradiction, this offers a new contradiction to answer step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is rejected because it contradicts itself on whether a removed tooth must be prepared before it counts as a utensil.

steps.title: אביי: with the base or without the base
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the second contradiction. A tooth removed with its base can be used right away, so it needs no preparing. A tooth removed without its base needs preparing first.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: But what is the difficulty? Perhaps this ruling is about teeth removed with their base, and that ruling is about teeth removed without their base.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the second contradiction too, by saying the two clauses describe different kinds of removed teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tooth that came out together with its base is ready to use, so it is a utensil even without preparing. A tooth that came out without its base is not usable yet, so it becomes a utensil only once it is prepared. That removes this contradiction as well, so the גמרא still needs a reason why the משנה is not authoritative.
steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts to find a contradiction in the comb משנה have now been pushed back by splitting the cases: inner versus outer teeth, and with base versus without base.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps this one is with their base,
phrases.notes: This is the clause saying no preparing is needed: the tooth came out with its base, so it is usable right away.

phrases.english: and that one is without their base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second contradiction from step 8 by placing the two clauses in different cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the contradiction about preparing a removed tooth. The גמרא still needs a reason why the משנה is not authoritative, and step 11 gives it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction assumes both clauses are about the same kind of tooth, but one may be a tooth with its base and the other a tooth without it.

steps.title: רב פפא: Thin Teeth Versus Thick Teeth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the second contradiction is no real problem. One clause speaks about thin teeth and the other about thick teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What is the difficulty? Maybe this clause is about thin teeth, and that clause is about thick teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the second contradiction in the comb משנה. He offers his own way to explain why the two clauses do not clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, one clause said a removed tooth is טמא without preparing, and another clause said it needs preparing. רב פפא says the two clauses may be talking about different teeth. A thin tooth needs no preparing, while a thick tooth must be prepared before it can be used. This takes away the second reason for rejecting the משנה, so the גמרא will need a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (a way of saying the problem is not real)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And what is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: He means the second contradiction from step 8, about whether a removed tooth needs preparing.

phrases.english: Perhaps this clause is about thin teeth,
and that clause is about thick teeth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction that אביי answered in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the second contradiction (step 8) as a reason to call the משנה not authoritative.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two clauses can be talking about different kinds of teeth (thin versus thick), so they never clashed.

steps.title: The Real Reason: The משנה Is רבי שמעון's View
steps.stepSummary: The real reason the comb משנה is not followed is that careful teachers end it with 'This is רבי שמעון'. So it is one Sage's opinion, not an unattributed ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that the careful teachers end this משנה with: 'This is רבי שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since both contradictions have been solved, the גמרא gives its final answer to the question from step 5. The משנה is not authoritative because it is רבי שמעון's opinion alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was never about a mistake in the משנה. Careful teachers add at the end that it follows רבי שמעון. A משנה with no name usually counts as the accepted law, but one marked as a single Sage's view does not carry that weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answers and gives a new one)
They conclude or end it with
The careful ones, teachers who repeat the text exactly

steps.whatToRemember: The comb משנה is not followed because it is the opinion of רבי שמעון alone. It is not rejected because of a contradiction inside it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the contradictions were left standing. Each one was answered (steps 7, 9 and 10), and that is exactly why the גמרא needed a different reason.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the careful teachers end it with:
This is the view of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradictions are answered, this gives the final reason the משנה is not authoritative.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is not authoritative because it follows רבי שמעון alone, as the careful teachers say at its end.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The comb משנה is a single Sage's opinion (רבי שמעון), so it is not treated as the accepted law.

steps.title: Betrothal Is Allowed During the Three Months
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין sent a ruling that a woman may be betrothed during her three-month waiting period, and that this is followed in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין sent word: One may betroth a woman within the three months, and this is how people act in practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבי חייא בר אבין rules that betrothal is allowed during the three-month waiting period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the opening unnamed opinion forbids both betrothal and marriage for three months. רבי יוסי allows betrothal. רבי חייא בר אבין rules that betrothal is allowed inside the three months, which matches רבי יוסי. The words 'and so one acts in practice' show this is the working הלכה and not just theory.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent (a ruling sent by message)
One may betroth (אירוסין, the first stage of marriage)
And so one acts in practice

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical הלכה in the משנה's dispute: betrothal is allowed during the three months, as רבי יוסי holds, and only marriage must wait.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin sent word:
One may betroth within three months,
phrases.notes: This is the three-month waiting period from the משנה, before a woman may marry again.

phrases.english: and so one acts in practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It goes back to the three-month waiting rule of the משנה and leaves the comb discussion behind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal is allowed during the three-month waiting period, and this is the practice.

steps.title: How the Three Months Are Counted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא הגדול, teaches that the three months count as most of the first month, most of the third month, and the whole middle month.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי אלעזר would teach us in the name of רבי חנינא הגדול: most of the first month, most of the third month, and the whole middle month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second teaching tied to the three months. It explains how to count them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three full months are not needed. Most of the first month and most of the third month are enough, as long as the middle month is complete. This tells us exactly when the 'three months' are over.
steps.whatToRemember: Betrothal is allowed during the three months. The three months are counted as most of the first, the whole second, and most of the third.

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Elazar would teach us
in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina the Great:
the majority of the first month,
and the majority of the third month,
and the middle month complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מְלַמְּדֵנוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the three months from step 12 and explains how they are counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three months are counted as most of the first month, the whole middle month, and most of the third month.

steps.title: אמימר allows betrothal on the ninetieth day
steps.stepSummary: אמימר permitted a woman to become betrothed on day 90 of her waiting period.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר allowed a woman to be betrothed on the ninetieth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical ruling: אמימר let a woman get betrothed on day 90 itself. This sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiting period is three months, which is roughly 90 days. אמימר holds that day 90 is already enough, so she does not need to wait for day 91 or later.

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted [a woman] to be betrothed
on the ninetieth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of how the three-month wait is counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal is permitted on day 90 of the waiting period.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that רב ושמואל require three full months not counting the day of death or the day of betrothal, so day 90 should be too early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But didn't רב ושמואל both say she must wait three months, not counting the day he died and not counting the day she gets betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's ruling by quoting a statement of רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If neither the day of death nor the day of betrothal counts, then betrothal on day 90 leaves fewer than 90 full days in between. That means אמימר's permission seems to go against רב ושמואל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But didn't Rav and Shmuel both say:
she needs to wait three months,
not counting the day on which he died
and not counting the day on which she is betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's permission to betroth on day 90.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first day and the last day both do not count, then day 90 does not complete the required period.

steps.title: That statement was about a nursing mother
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רב ושמואל's statement about not counting those days was said about a nursing mother's 24-month wait, not about the three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement was said about a nursing mother. רב ושמואל both said she must wait 24 months, not counting the day the baby was born and not counting the day she gets betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי and defends his ruling. The statement רב אשי quoted belongs to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of leaving out the first and last days was said about a מינקת, a nursing mother, who waits 24 months. So it says nothing about the three-month wait, and אמימר's day-90 ruling can still stand.

phrases.english: That was said regarding a nursing mother,
for Rav and Shmuel both said:
she needs to wait twenty-four months,
not counting the day on which [the baby] was born,
and not counting the day on which she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the quoted ruling to a different case (nursing mother instead of widow or divorcee).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל's rule applied to the three-month wait, which would forbid day 90.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their rule was about the 24-month nursing wait, so the three-month wait may end on day 90.

steps.title: A challenge from רבא's ruined feast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story: someone made a betrothal feast on day 90, and רבא made him lose it, which suggests day 90 is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was a man who made a betrothal feast on the ninetieth day, and רבא made his feast go to waste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר again, this time with a real-life case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא stopped a betrothal on day 90, then רבא held that day 90 is still too early, against אמימר.

phrases.english: But there was a certain man who made a betrothal feast
on the ninetieth day,
and Rava made him lose his feast!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָהוּא דַּעֲבַד סְעוּדַת אֵירוּסִין בְּיוֹם תִּשְׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to אמימר's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's permission to betroth on day 90.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא blocked a betrothal on day 90 in practice.

steps.title: That was a wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: The feast רבא stopped was for נישואין (full marriage), not אירוסין (betrothal).
steps.simpleTranslation: That feast was a marriage feast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the story-challenge: it was a different kind of feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's stopping the event does not prove anything about betrothal on day 90. It was about full marriage, so the challenge falls away.

phrases.english: That one was a marriage feast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא forbade a wedding on day 90; betrothal is not covered by that story.

steps.title: The final ruling on counting both waiting periods
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that both the 24-month nursing wait and the three-month wait leave out the first day and the day of betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: she must wait 24 months, not counting the day the baby was born and not counting the day she gets betrothed. And she must wait three months, not counting the day he died and not counting the day she gets betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for both waiting periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though אמימר's answers held up, the הלכה goes the other way: the rule of leaving out the first and last days applies to the three-month wait too. So in practice, betrothal on day 90 is not allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, for both a nursing mother (24 months) and a widow or divorcee (three months), neither the starting day nor the betrothal day counts toward the wait. That means אמימר's day-90 permission is not followed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the הלכה follows אמימר just because his answers in Steps 16 and 18 worked. Answering a challenge only shows a view is possible; the final ruling here goes the other way.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: she needs to wait
twenty-four months,
not counting the day on which [the baby] was born,
and not counting the day on which she is betrothed.
And she needs to wait three months,
not counting the day on which he died,
and not counting the day on which she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion and rules against אמימר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both waiting periods leave out the first day and the betrothal day, so betrothal on day 90 is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical counting rule for when a widow, a divorcee, or a nursing mother may become betrothed again.

steps.title: רב חסדא's argument that a widow should be allowed to become betrothed
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's exception for a widow, רב חסדא argues: if betrothal is allowed during a stricter mourning period when laundering is forbidden, then surely it is allowed during the widow's period, when laundering is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "except for a widow, etc." רב חסדא said a קל וחומר: If during a time when laundering is forbidden, betrothal is still allowed, then during a time when laundering is allowed, isn't it logical that betrothal is allowed too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה, where רבי יוסי excludes a widow from betrothal during her mourning. רב חסדא questions this with a קל וחומר; this sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering clothes is used as a measure of how strict a mourning period is. If even a stricter mourning period, when laundering is forbidden, allows betrothal, then the widow's milder period should allow it too. The גמרא will identify which period he means in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'how much more so' argument: if a rule holds in the harder case, it surely holds in the easier one

phrases.english: "Except for a widow, etc."
Rav Chisda said a kal vachomer:
If where it is forbidden to launder,
it is permitted to be betrothed,
then where it is permitted to launder,
isn't it logical that it is permitted to be betrothed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's exception for a widow.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה that a widow may not become betrothed during her mourning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: a stricter mourning period, where laundering is forbidden, still allows betrothal, so the widow's milder period should too.

steps.title: The sources behind רב חסדא's mourning-period argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the stricter mourning period רב חסדא meant. A משנה says laundering is forbidden in the week of תשעה באב. A ברייתא says that before this time people may betroth but not marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this stricter period? As the משנה teaches: in the week when תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to do laundry, but on Thursday it is allowed out of respect for שבת. And a ברייתא teaches: before this time, people cut back on their activities: on business, building and planting. They may get betrothed but may not get married, and they do not make a betrothal feast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing where רב חסדא got his proof. It brings two sources that together show that betrothal is allowed even in a time when laundering is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the week of תשעה באב is strict, since laundering is forbidden. The ברייתא says that 'before this time' betrothal is still allowed. At this point the גמרא reads 'before this time' as those same strict days, which gives רב חסדא the base for his קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The ninth of Av, the fast day of mourning for the בית המקדש
Literally 'to take and to give': doing business

phrases.english: What is it? As we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: "It" is the stricter mourning period רב חסדא mentioned, when laundering is forbidden.

phrases.english: The week in which the Ninth of Av falls
phrases.notes: Here שַׁבָּת means the whole week, not just the day of שבת.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder
but on Thursday it is permitted
out of respect for Shabbat.
And it was taught in a baraita: Before this time
phrases.notes: For now, the גמרא takes 'before this time' to mean the strict days right before תשעה באב.

phrases.english: the people reduce their activities,
refraining from business dealings,
from building and from planting.
And they may betroth, but they may not marry,
and they do not make a betrothal feast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the sources for the stricter period that רב חסדא's קל וחומר in step 20 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's premise that betrothal is allowed even in a period when laundering is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תענית about the week of תשעה באב, combined with a ברייתא about the time 'before this time'.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks about an earlier, lighter period
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא allowing betrothal is speaking about the time before the week of תשעה באב, not the strict week itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was speaking about the time 'before the before.' That means the days before the week of תשעה באב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי by rereading the ברייתא. Betrothal is allowed only in the earlier, lighter days, not in the strict week when laundering is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's proof needed betrothal to be allowed in the same period when laundering is forbidden. If the ברייתא is about an earlier period when laundering is allowed, that link breaks. Then the קל וחומר from step 20 no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'before the before': the period before the week of תשעה באב

phrases.english: When that baraita was taught,
it was taught about the time before the before.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. 'Before the before' means the days before the week of תשעה באב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rereads the ברייתא from step 21 to take away the basis of רב חסדא's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the time frame of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'before this time' meant the strict week of תשעה באב, when laundering is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the earlier days before that week, so it says nothing about betrothal in a period when laundering is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא builds a new קל וחומר from the earlier period
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even the earlier period gives a קל וחומר. If betrothal is allowed when business is forbidden, it is surely allowed for a widow, who may do business.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even from the 'before the before' period there is a קל וחומר. If in a time when doing business is forbidden, betrothal is still allowed, then in a time when doing business is allowed, isn't it logical that betrothal is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the new reading of the ברייתא. But he shows that the same challenge against רבי יוסי still works, just with a different comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the earlier period, business is forbidden, yet betrothal is allowed. A widow in her mourning period for her husband is allowed to do business, so her situation is lighter. So she should surely be allowed to get betrothed, which goes against רבי יוסי's exception.

keyTerms.meaning: also. רבא is saying the same kind of argument works here too
if... (the opening word of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Also from the 'before the before' period there is an a fortiori argument:
If in a situation where it is forbidden to do business
it is permitted to become betrothed,
then in a situation where it is permitted to do business
phrases.notes: He means the widow's mourning period for her husband, when business is allowed.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that it is permitted to become betrothed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer from step 22 and builds a new version of the same challenge from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that a widow may not get betrothed during her three months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier period forbids business but allows betrothal. The widow's period allows business, so betrothal must surely be allowed for her too.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's statement is about marriage, not betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רבא's challenge and changes the wording. רבי יוסי said all women may get married within three months except a widow, so a widow may still get betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say that רבי יוסי says 'all women may get betrothed.' Rather, say: 'all women may get married.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question by changing the wording of רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new wording, רבי יוסי's exception for a widow applies only to marriage (נישואין) during the three months. Betrothal (אירוסין) is allowed for her too, so רבא's קל וחומר no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not say... rather say': the גמרא is changing the wording of a statement

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, a widow may get betrothed during her three months even according to רבי יוסי. His exception for her is only about marriage. The קל וחומר from the mourning before תשעה באב is what forced this change in wording.
steps.confusionAlert: אירוסין (betrothal) and נישואין (full marriage) are two different stages. The whole back-and-forth here depends on which stage רבי יוסי meant.

phrases.english: Do not say

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְאָרְסוּ,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei says: All women may become betrothed,
rather, say:
All women may get married.
phrases.notes: So the widow is left out only from marriage. She may still get betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְאָרְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's קל וחומר and resolves it by changing the wording of רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's statement is about marriage. A widow may not marry within three months, but she may get betrothed.
